record.title: Burundi restrictions on Rwanda border following political crisis
record.crossings: Ruhwa; Kanyaru-Haut/Akanyaru Haut; Gasenyi-Nemba/Nemba (evidence differs by phase).
record.direction: Burundian controls restricted both entry and exit in observed March 2022 cases; no uniform direction established for entire regime.
record.movement: Passenger and small-trader restrictions varied by phase. March 2022 field reporting includes outbound Burundian traders, Burundian returnees and outbound Rwandans; later agency-vehicle transit was permitted.
record.exceptions: Reported agency-vehicle entry/exit permission from Bukavu via Rwanda dated 29 August 2022 (RTNK; original order not retrieved). Burundi Eco issue 521, printed 2 September 2022, more specifically describes an Interior ministry letter of 29 August to the national police inspector general instructing permission for Mapassa Car Transit via Ruhwa for its Congolese and Burundian clients coming from DRC through Rwanda. Burundi Eco 16 September field reporting describes those passengers at Ruhwa. These preceded general ministry-permit relaxation observed 30 September.
record.enforcement: SOS reporters observed 30 September crossing without former ministry permission at Kanyaru-Hautand Ruhwa; Gasenyı-Nemba applied relaxation later that day.
record.official_rationale: Burundi demanded extradition of people it accused of the 2015 coup attempt.
record.context: Retrospective reports describe a prolonged closure spanning political tensions and COVID restrictions.
record.uncertainty: Onset and continuity unresolved. 2020 traveller reports show earlier selective access. 30 September 2022 is documented relaxation atnamedposts, with one witness hearing opening previous evening. Government still denied formal opening then; ministry acknowledged opening22/25 October. Earlier limited bus transit means 30 September is not the first reopening of every category. 29 August is a reported permission date, not an observed first crossing. Official March 2022 statement supports political context, not a uniform continuous closure. The newly inspected Burundi Eco brief reports the letter but is not the original administrative instrument. UMUSEKE contemporary Kinyarwanda reporting corroborates March 2022 restrictions at Ruhwa; its retrospective 2016 reference does not resolve onset or continuity.
